sentences.text:
This application has been filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.163/2023 registered at Police Station- Tamiya, District Chhindwara (M.P.)
for commission of offence under Sections 376, 376(3), 376(D)(a), 376(2)(n), 376(2)(f), 506 of IPC and Section 5/6, 5(g)/6, 5(j)1/6 of POCSO Act.
2. As per the prosecution story, it is alleged that present applicant and other co-accused person have committed rape with a minor girl.
The police officer has completed the investigation and charge sheet has been filed.
3 . Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
It is submitted that both the parties have entered into compromise and mother of the prosecutrix has also executed an affidavit in favour of the applicant.
The applicant has no criminal past.
The trial would take considerable time, therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be granted bail.

Learned counsel for the applicant has placed reliance in the case of Brijesh Singh Thakur Vs. State of M.P. & Anr. bearing MCRC No.39860 of 2023 passed by co-ordinate Bench of this Court on 16.02.2024.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail and submitted that at the time of incident prosecutrix was minor girl aged about 13 years and the applicant with co-accused Pawan committed gang rape with the her.
Applicant is the step-brother of the prosecutrix.
It is further submitted that statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. in which she has stated against applicant and co-accused person Pawan.

5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, the prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident and applicant along with other co-accused person committed gang rape with her therefore, looking to the seriousness of the offence, I am not inclined to grant bail to the present applicant.
